title: The Farmer and the Viper
text:
One bitter winter day a farmer was walking home across his frozen fields when he saw a snake lying on the ground, stiff and almost dead from the cold.

He knew perfectly well what kind of snake it was. Even so he felt sorry for it. He picked it up, opened his coat and put it against his chest to warm it with his own body, and carried it home.

As the warmth soaked into the snake, it began to stir. Its strength came back, and with it its nature. It raised its head and bit the man who had saved it.

The farmer knew the bite was fatal. As he sank down he said, "I deserve this, for showing pity to a creature that was wicked from the start."
lesson: Compassion is good, but it is not the same as naive trust. Before you take someone close, look at how they have treated others.
